academicDiscussion.courseTitle: Teaching and Learning in Higher Education
academicDiscussion.professorPost: This week we are looking at how assessment shapes learning. Some universities allow every student to resubmit a marked essay once: the student reads the tutor's feedback, revises the same essay, and can receive a higher mark in the same course. Other universities treat the first mark as final. What do you think? Should a university let every student resubmit a marked essay once for a higher mark? Why or why not?

studentPosts.name: Priya
studentPosts.post: I think resubmission should be allowed. At the moment most of us read the mark, skim the comments, and move on. If I could revise the same essay, I would actually have to put my tutor's feedback to use, and that is when I would learn how to build a better argument.

studentPosts.name: Tomas
studentPosts.post: I disagree. A mark should show what a student can do on a first attempt, and that is what makes marks comparable from one student to the next. A revised essay partly reflects the tutor's own suggestions. Resubmission would also give tutors a second round of marking, leaving them less time for everyone else.
